dana: Quick heads-up — I'm putting up a short proposal to tighten who can request SIEM exports and how long those exports live. Main changes: rotate bastion/export tokens to short TTLs, require KMS unwrap via a scoped CMK for any export, and enforce a 30d retention cut for exports created by JIT requests. Planning to roll this out next Wed. Thoughts? :eyes:

maria: Could you paste the exact token TTL / rotation cadence you're proposing? also need thoughts on how this impacts incident triage when we need >30d evidence.

dana: Proposed: bastion/export tokens TTL=12h, automated rotation every 6h (staggered). JIT export leases still allow extended evidence grabs via a legal/IR exception flow (ticket + 2nd approver) — that would keep artifacts for up to 180d but gated.

sean: On RBAC mapping: who maps to the 'export:read' role? Right now the role is broad (oncall, sec-analyst, infra-eng). Suggest split: `export:read:triage` (oncall + sec-analyst), `export:read:forensics` (forensic-team + legal). That lets us audit by role.

aj: Agree on role split. A couple notes re audit logs: every unwrap operation (KMS decrypt) + every presigned URL generation needs to emit an immutable event with requestor, approver (if any), ticket id, and artifact digests. Otherwise we lose provenance. We should include the KMS key-id in the logs.

security-bot: New policy draft uploaded: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-3421 (policy doc, includes sample KMS CMK policy and event schema). :link:

maria: For the KMS unwrap gating, are we planning to use a proxy service or direct CMK grants? I prefer proxy with short-lived unwrap token so we keep key access limited.

dana: Proxy model — exporter service performs unwrap after checking role + ticket. Proxy will request CMK Decrypt with a service account; CMK policy only allows Decrypt from that service account when the request includes a signed approval token from our approval service. That way the CMK isn't directly grantable to humans.

sean: Implementation note: add `approvalToken` field that includes approver, expiry, and ticket hash. Approval service signs it with its own key. Then exporter proxies it to KMS with condition `kms:EncryptionContext:approval=sha256(ticket)` in CMK policy.

aj: Also, ensure export artifacts in S3 are encrypted with the same CMK and use bucket lifecycle to purge at TTL. For JIT-case, mark object metadata `redwood:export-lease=JIT:<expiry>` so lifecycle can clean up.

ops-bot: deploy bot: created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4812 — adds rotation cron + audit-event plumbing. :robot_face:

maria: Two operational concerns: 1) incident playbook needs a fast bypass path (phone call + IAM emergency role) for live-high-severity IR — how do we avoid bypass abuse? 2) Will this increase our latency for urgent exports?

dana: 1) Bypass: limited to SRE lead + CISO oncall, action logged and auto-revoked after 1h. We also capture a call record and require postmortem. 2) Latency: proxy adds ~150ms for unwrap; presigned URL generation another ~50ms. We can cache approval tokens for repeating queries within 5m to reduce overhead.

sean: We'll need a migration plan to re-label existing exports with lease metadata and backfill KMS encryption if objects used legacy key. Propose migration window 30d with read-only fallback to old artifacts during migration.

aj: QA checklist: unit tests for approvalToken validation, e2e for exporter->kms flow, replay test for audit events, and a chaos test that forces CMK deny to confirm fallbacks.

maria: Adding: update runbook for oncall with exact steps to request legal exception (ticket template + 2nd approver), and a sample Slack workflow to surface requests to CISO oncall.

dana: Action items: (1) I’ll update the policy doc with RBAC splits and exception flow (SEC-3421) — due EOD tomorrow. (2) @sean to prototype approvalToken schema and CMK condition — target Tue. (3) @aj to add audit-event schema + lifecycle rules — target Tue. (4) ops-bot PR linked above — review please.

sean: ack, I'll slot time Tue morning.

aj: ack, will add tests and lifecycle rules.

maria: ack. I'll draft the runbook once the exception flow is finalized.

security-bot: Note: we should run a tabletop IR drill after rollout to validate the bypass + logging. Recommend scheduling in next oncall cycle.

dana: +1. If no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll merge the policy and kick off the PR reviews. :thumbsup:

sean: +1 from me.

aj: +1.

maria: +1.

ops-bot: CI: all checks passed for PR #4812 — branch ready for review.

dana: Thanks team — filing follow-ups and moving to staging.
